systems.name: rubric-d-failure-paths

lens.name: silent-failures
lens.focus: Error handling and fallbacks. List every catch, .catch, default-on-error, optional chaining or ?? fallback, retry, timeout and early return that the change adds or touches. For each, ask: which unexpected errors could it hide; did the request or spec ask for this fallback; should the failure propagate or fail closed instead; is a retry limited to transient failures, bounded by one deadline, and does it keep the original failure and its classification; does every pending or in-flight state end on every path. A failed security, isolation or inspection check that ends in silent success or an unchecked path is a blocker.

lens.name: test-gaps
lens.focus: Tests. For each new or changed behaviour, find the test that would fail if that behaviour regressed, and say so when none exists. Flag tests that assert the defect they should catch, compare the code with itself, mock away the logic under test, pass for the wrong reason (invalid fixture, swallowed error, early return, wrong file), or were weakened, skipped or special-cased to pass. Name the missing or broken test case precisely. A test gap that hides a real defect in the change is at least major; report the underlying defect itself as its own finding.

lens.name: trust-boundaries
lens.focus: Secrets, untrusted input and isolation. Trace every credential, token, private value and untrusted input (issue or PR text, gate or test output, model output, configuration or scripts from the change) from its source to every sink: logs, events, errors, PR comments, commit metadata, branch names, model prompts, files and network. Check that redaction happens after decoding and before truncation, on error and retry paths as well as the normal one. Check sandbox profiles, deny lists and allowlists for path aliases, symlinks, files versus directories, environment variables and child processes. Anything that steers the factory must come from the base commit, never the change. When isolation or a check cannot be confirmed, the code must refuse with a clear reason, never fall back silently.

lens.name: requirements
lens.focus: Requirements. Restate each requirement, acceptance criterion and universal clause (every, all, never, only, ordering, on resume or restart) from the request and the specification. For each one, find the code that implements it on every entry point: resume paths, both harness backends, the daemon and scripts/, CLI and HTTP, cache-side calls. Mark it implemented, partly implemented or missing. Every missing or partly implemented clause that the request states is a finding that quotes the clause. A clause only the specification adds, which the request does not need, is at most minor.

systems.severityRubric:
# Severity by consequence and trigger (the reviewer's severity is not an input you must keep)
For each candidate ask: "would this plausibly happen in the next month of normal factory operation?" Deploys restart the daemon daily, so restart windows count unless they last milliseconds.
- critical: a realistic trigger that loses or corrupts persisted state, leaks a secret or private data, breaks a trust or confinement boundary, or stops the factory or deploys.
- high: a realistic trigger with real harm: a wrong result, a silent failure, lost or repeated work, a check the change claims to add that a realistic input bypasses, or a compatibility break with the previous release.
- medium: a real defect with a contrived trigger (an unusual input, configuration, environment or timing the request does not ask to handle), or a cost only in tests or diagnostics, such as a missing or weak test on its own, or a missing or less informative log line or error message.
- low: cosmetic, a process ask (a report, measurements, PR text), or behaviour the repository's own rules adopt.
A secret or credential stored or shown unredacted is at least high whatever the trigger. A new test that fails in normal runs stops deploys, so it is at least high.
Requirements: a requirement counts as undelivered only when the behaviour or protection it exists for is missing at head; then rate the missing behaviour by its trigger and harm like any other defect. Different wording, a different mechanism than the one the request preferred, log or message text, and places the request does not name are not undelivered requirements. Edits outside the request's scope are not an undelivered requirement either.
Failure paths are realistic triggers, not contrived ones: a failed read, command or network call, a lost response, a crash or restart, a concurrent change between two reads of shared state, and timestamps that share a second all happen in normal factory operation. A failure path the request explicitly asks the change to handle is a realistic trigger however rare it is.
A digest, report, status or feed the change produces that omits or misstates items is a wrong result, not a diagnostics cost.

Verifier: 6 candidates, 6 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

verification.evidence: src/router/router.ts:167-168: `const origin = originExclusion(m, this.excludeOrigins); if (origin) throw new Error(...)`. src/evals/runner.ts:617 calls `router.toTarget(model, effort ?? null)` before the trial's `try` at line 625. The worker catches the rejection at lines 499-502 with `failed = true; throw error;`; line 524 calls `store.interruptEval(run.id, (error as Error).message, "failed")`.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, patch a queued model from US to CN before its trial reaches target construction. The exception escapes trial-level handling, stops new trials for that provider, marks the eval failed, and skips remaining queued trials.

findings.title: Verifier failure can omit the exclusion that exhausted the choices
findings.detail: The exclusion reason is propagated only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but is ineligible because it raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternative. The invocation therefore fails without the required origin exclusion reason.
findings.suggestion: Include collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, and log excluded verifier choices.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an allowed model that raised the candidate and a CN model excluded by configuration. No verifier can be selected, but the error reports only that the allowed model raised the candidate.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1342 collects `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`)`, but :1347 reports them only under `if (!listed.length && exclusions.length)`. With an allowed model remaining, :1349 calls `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:325–327 then throws `NoCapacityError(`verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`)` without the exclusions.
verification.trigger: The verifier roster contains an excluded CN model and an allowed model that raised the candidate. The allowed model keeps listed nonempty, then independence selection fails; the error omits the CN exclusion.

findings.title: Cover a catalog origin change while a production invocation is waiting
findings.detail: The new queued-origin tests exercise eval and chat calls, but no test covers a normal pipeline invocation whose selected runtime model becomes excluded while it waits for a provider slot or before dispatch. The existing pipeline race tests change routing cells or provider preference, so they would not catch a regression in catalog-driven routing invalidation.
findings.suggestion: Add a fake-harness pipeline test that selects an allowed runtime model, blocks it before dispatch, patches its origin to an excluded value, and verifies that it is never invoked and the exclusion reason is reported.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model is changed from US to CN while a production run is queued. If catalog edits stop invalidating the routing revision, the stale target can be dispatched despite the configured CN exclusion without an existing test failing.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline.test.ts:9484 tests queued edits only with `test.each(["cell", "prefer"])`; lines 9497–9498 call `runtime.setCell(...)` or `runtime.setPrefer(...)`, never a catalog origin patch. Production currently relies on src/router/runtime-catalog.ts:71, `this.router.setModels(this.models)`, and src/router/router.ts:79, `this.invalidateRouting()`. src/pipeline/context.ts:742 guards dispatch with `if (revision.aborted)`, rather than rechecking the model's current origin.
verification.trigger: Coverage gap: removing catalog-change routing invalidation would allow a production invocation queued for a US model to dispatch after its catalog origin changes to excluded CN. Existing queued production tests exercise policy and preference changes, not this catalog mutation. The current implementation prevents the bypass.

findings.title: Verifier exclusions are omitted from the run log
findings.detail: The request says the skip reason in the run log reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. This verifier-selection path removes excluded alternatives before calling the router, but logs their reasons only when every listed target is excluded. When an allowed verifier remains, the exclusion is invisible in the run log.
findings.suggestion: Record the excluded verifier alternatives and their reasons when filtering them, including when another verifier is selected.
findings.failure_scenario: A review system lists one CN verifier and one US verifier with CN excluded; the US verifier runs, but the run log does not explain that the CN verifier was skipped.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1341–1343 handles excluded verifiers with `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`); return [];` without logging. At :1350 only the selected verifier reaches `call(request, { ...constraints, only }, undefined)`. src/router/router.ts:386–388 routes that request through `consider([c.only]); return { candidates: ranked.map((r) => r.target), skipped };`, so the excluded roster entries never reach the `skipped: decision.skipped` log metadata in src/pipeline/context.ts:659–661.
verification.trigger: A verifier roster contains an excluded CN model and an eligible US model. The US verifier runs, but the CN verifier was filtered before routing and its exclusion is absent from the verifier invocation log.

findings.title: Verifier exhaustion can hide the origin exclusion reason
findings.detail: The request says that when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with the origin exclusion reason. This check reports exclusions only if the filtered list is empty. If the remaining allowed targets are ineligible because they raised the finding, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternatives and their reasons.
findings.suggestion: Include the collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after applying the independence constraints.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an excluded CN model and an allowed US model, and the US model raised the candidate being verified. Selection fails with only the raised-candidate message, despite the CN exclusion preventing the other choice.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1347 throws the collected exclusion reasons only when `!listed.length`; :1349 otherwise invokes `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:323–327 rejects remaining models that raised the candidate and throws only `verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`.
verification.trigger: An excluded CN verifier is removed while an allowed US verifier remains but raised the candidate. Selection fails with the raised-candidate message and loses the origin exclusion reason. This is the same defect as C2.

findings.title: Reviewable text still requires a binary allowance in some mode changes
findings.detail: The new condition applies a stricter definition of text than Git's diff classification. It flags executable text containing non-UTF-8 bytes or control characters, and flags executable text under a media extension regardless of its contents. It also newly blocks a non-UTF-8 text file when an edit removes its executable bit: the old condition did not flag a mode change accompanied by a content change. These paths can be shown as text in the diff but are reported as binary content.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the mode condition to removing the inert-media exemption, and leave text classification to the existing diff classification as requested.

findings.title: The stop assertion still depends on a fixed scheduling window
findings.detail: After releasing the gate, the test waits 800 ms and assumes any surviving check has written `end`. On a sufficiently loaded runner, a check that survived `stop()` can remain unscheduled until after the assertion, allowing the test to pass even though interruption failed. The restart test likewise can finish its log assertion before a surviving old check gets scheduled. This leaves the requested failure detection dependent on timing.
findings.suggestion: Use an observable process or completion handshake that establishes the original check has terminated before asserting its log, without relying on a fixed delay.
findings.failure_scenario: If `stop()` returns while the gate subprocess survives, and that subprocess is delayed for more than 800 ms after the release file is created, the first test observes only `start` and passes.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:687–688 releases the gate with `writeFileSync(gateReleasePath(), "");` then waits `await Bun.sleep(800);`. verification.trigger: If a regressed stop() returns with a surviving gate subprocess, and that subprocess remains unscheduled through the wait and assertion, the test passes without detecting the surviving check.

findings.failure_scenario: Stop returns without interrupting the gate, but the gate process is not scheduled until after the 800 ms wait and assertion; the test passes despite the gate later writing `end`.

findings.title: Draft deferrals never resume when GitHub polling is disabled
findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.
findings.suggestion: Provide a change-observation path for installations with polling disabled, or preserve a bounded fallback for that configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/index.ts:38-45 starts `startGitHubPoller(...)` only when `factory.cfg.githubPoll` is true. src/db/store.ts:1114 selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`; draft triggers become `state = 'skipped'` with reason `"PR is draft"` (1177-1191). src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`. The sole caller of `recheckDraftConflictTriggers` is the poller (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373-374).
verification.trigger: With github.poll = false, a land conflict trigger is deferred while its PR is draft. Marking that PR ready on the same head leaves the trigger skipped indefinitely; subsequent conflict processing cannot start its round.

candidates.title: A head change can be missed while a draft lookup is in flight
candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. If the poller saves the new head before an in-flight live lookup marks an older-head trigger as draft, subsequent polls see the same head and never call recheckDraftConflictTriggers, even though that method would detect the mismatch against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: A land trigger is immediately evaluated against any saved poller snapshot, even if that snapshot predates the approved head. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when the saved head differs, and a later poll cannot reconsider it. The queue has already blocked the entry, so the requested conflict round never starts.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before rejecting a land trigger for a stale head, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A; a review round pushes head B and B is approved before the next poll. Landing B conflicts with the base, but the saved snapshot still says A, so the B trigger is permanently skipped as `PR head moved`.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:16–21 reads the saved snapshot and executes `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now())` without refreshing it. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 selects `"PR head moved"` when `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head`; lines 1137–1140 permanently update the trigger to `state = 'skipped'`. A later poll can create a separate replacement trigger.
verification.trigger: Saved head A plus a land conflict trigger for approved head B causes the B land trigger to be permanently skipped rather than started or retained pending.

findings.title: A conflict observed during another round is lost permanently
findings.detail: An active review or conflict round causes the trigger to be marked skipped. The poller emits `pr.conflicting` only on entry into the conflicting state, so if the active round fails or ends without changing the head, subsequent polls do not create another trigger. The unresolved conflict therefore never gets its own round.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while another round is active and reconsider it when that round terminates, subject to a fresh PR observation and the daily cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is in flight when the poller first observes the PR as CONFLICTING. The trigger is skipped; the review round later fails without pushing, and every subsequent poll still sees CONFLICTING, so no conflict round starts.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1130–1131 rejects any nonterminal round: `rounds.some((r) => !TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(r.status)) ? "round in flight"`. Lines 1137–1141 permanently consume that trigger with `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. Only pending triggers are retried (src/db/store.ts:1071: `WHERE state = 'pending'`). Subsequent unchanged observations emit no replacement: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 requires `next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING"` to emit `pr.conflicting`.
verification.trigger: An eligible open factory PR first becomes CONFLICTING while a review round is active. Its conflict trigger is marked skipped. If the review round fails without pushing and subsequent polls keep reporting CONFLICTING on the same head, no conflict round starts, including after restart.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: The land path uses any stored GitHub snapshot without refreshing it. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when that snapshot's head differs from the land entry's approved head, even if the snapshot is simply older than the approval. The trigger is then no longer pending, so this landing-queue trigger cannot recover on restart.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or otherwise establish the snapshot's freshness before permanently skipping a land trigger; retain it pending when the observation cannot establish the current head.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saved head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, and the land queue detects a conflict at B. Processing compares B with the saved A and skips the trigger instead of starting a round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 passes an existing saved snapshot directly to `startConflictTrigger`. src/db/store.ts:1099 obtains `seen` from `githubPrData`; lines 1126–1127 classify the stale A versus trigger B mismatch as `"PR head moved"`; lines 1137–1140 persist `state = 'skipped'`. Subsequent processing selects only pending triggers (src/db/store.ts:1069).
verification.trigger: The PR advances from saved A to approved B before polling catches up; landing B conflicts, and its durable land trigger is discarded. A separate future poller trigger may recover the work.

findings.title: Retrying comment creation can post duplicate resolution comments
findings.detail: The `gh` wrapper retries transient failures around the entire comment command. If GitHub creates the comment but its response is lost, the retry creates another comment without checking the marker again. The preflight marker lookup only protects a later delivery attempt, not retries within this call.
findings.suggestion: Recheck for the marker after an uncertain comment outcome before issuing another creation request.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts `pr comment`, but the client receives a timeout or connection reset; the retry posts a second comment with the same conflict-round marker.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1921-1922 wraps each gh command in `withGitHubRetry(async () => (await runner(args, signal, stdin)) ?? "", ...)`. The marker lookup happens once at :1892-1894, before `await gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, text)` at :1899. src/git/repos.ts:93-97 retries transient failures without repeating that lookup.
verification.trigger: GitHub creates the comment but its acknowledgement is lost through a retryable connection error, with retry budget remaining. The command retries directly and creates a duplicate resolution comment.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the PR delivery grant
findings.detail: The new auto-merge mutation occurs before `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush` verify that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected branch and repository, and matches the round's current grant. A stale or invalid round can therefore modify the PR even though delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head branch changes while a conflict round runs and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the changed branch.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 executes `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.autoMerge) await gh(["pr", "merge", prUrl, "--disable-auto"], ctx.signal)`. Only afterward, at :1869-1870, it calls `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. src/core/delivery.ts:88 rejects a changed branch: `if (pr.headBranch !== branch) return ...`.
verification.trigger: The PR switches head branches while the round runs and has auto-merge enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge before rejecting the branch mismatch, leaving an unrelated current head's merge configuration changed.

findings.title: Restart tests do not cover a stale saved observation
findings.detail: The restart tests use either no saved observation or one matching the trigger. They therefore pass while a saved observation for an older head causes a durable land trigger to be skipped permanently, and while an outdated open, non-draft observation can start an ineligible round.
findings.suggestion: Add restart and land-trigger cases with an older saved head and with a PR that became draft or closed after the saved observation. Assert that a current observation governs whether the trigger starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending trigger for head B is recovered while the database still contains an open CONFLICTING snapshot for head A; the existing tests never exercise this state.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:330–340 records a trigger and reopens the database without saving a PR observation. The other startup test uses the same head for both: line 517 records `await remoteHead()` and line 525 saves `headRefOid: await remoteHead()`. Neither exercises mismatched heads. This matters because src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 checks `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head` and assigns `"PR head moved"`; lines 1137–1140 persist the trigger as `skipped`.
verification.trigger: Recover a pending trigger for head B with a saved OPEN/CONFLICTING observation for head A. Recovery skips the trigger; the existing restart tests do not exercise or detect this outcome.

findings.title: The non-factory polling case bypasses the poller
findings.detail: The non-factory branch inserts a trigger and calls the store consumer directly, so it does not test whether polling a non-factory PR creates a round. A regression in tracking, event generation, or poller consumption for that case would still pass the test.
findings.suggestion: Exercise a tracked non-factory PR through the same fake GitHub poller path as the other eligibility cases and assert that no conflict round starts.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller erroneously starts a conflict round for a non-factory PR, but the test bypasses the poller and continues to pass.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:365–371 handles `eligibility === "non-factory"` by directly calling `recordConflictTrigger(...)` and `startConflictTrigger(...)`. The `startGitHubPoller(...)` call at lines 372–373 is inside the alternative `else` branch. The assertion at line 393 therefore tests the store consumer, without running the poller for the non-factory case.
verification.trigger: A regression affecting non-factory PR handling in the polling path would remain undetected by this case because it invokes only the store methods.

findings.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
findings.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing paths before storing them or sending them to any external sink, while retaining whatever representation is needed for local conflict resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed repository contains a conflicting filename that includes a registered token; the token is stored in conflictFiles in the run state.

verification.evidence: src/git/merge.ts:79-83 obtains and returns filenames from `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U -z`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:2245 assigns `ctx.state.conflictFiles = conflicts`, then :2252 persists it with `ctx.store.updateRun(..., ctx.state)`. src/db/store.ts:1484-1486 serializes the state using `values.push(json(state))`, without credential redaction.
verification.trigger: A conflicting filename contains a registered credential. The raw filename is persisted in run state; redacting the later resolution comment does not protect that stored value.

findings.detail: The new GitHub mutation runs before stored() and assertFactoryBranchPush validate that the grant still holds and that the PR is still open on the expected branch and head. A stale conflict round can therefore change auto-merge settings even when its delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and recheck state after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head or round grant changes while a conflict round is running and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the stale round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 disables auto-merge before :1869 invokes `stored()` and :1870 invokes `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. The stored-record mismatch throws at :1857; src/core/delivery.ts:77-80 rejects remote or GitHub head mismatches.

findings.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment
findings.detail: The idempotency check accepts the marker in any PR comment without verifying its author. A PR participant can post the predictable marker before delivery, causing the factory to treat the required resolution summary as already published.
findings.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1891 constructs `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:${ctx.run.id} -->`; :1892-1894 reads comments as `{ body?: string }[]` and skips publication whenever `comments?.some((comment) => comment.body?.includes(marker))`. No author or provenance check is performed.
verification.trigger: A participant posts a comment containing the round's marker before delivery. The merge is pushed, but the participant's comment suppresses the factory's resolution summary.

candidates.detail: The land-trigger consumer treats any saved GitHub snapshot as current and immediately consumes the trigger. If the saved head differs from the approved head that the queue just found conflicting, `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped. A later poll that still sees `CONFLICTING` does not emit another `pr.conflicting` event if the previous snapshot was already conflicting, so no round starts. The same stale snapshot can also start a round for a PR that has since become a draft or closed.
candidates.suggestion: Verify land triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and retain the trigger when the observation cannot establish its eligibility.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last recorded head A as CONFLICTING; the PR advances to head B, which also conflicts, and the land queue blocks B before the next poll. The trigger for B is skipped as moved, and the next CONFLICTING observation emits no new event.

candidates.title: Restart tests do not cover a stale saved observation
candidates.detail: The restart tests use either no saved observation or one matching the trigger. They therefore pass while a saved observation for an older head causes a durable land trigger to be skipped permanently, and while an outdated open, non-draft observation can start an ineligible round.
candidates.suggestion: Add restart and land-trigger cases with an older saved head and with a PR that became draft or closed after the saved observation. Assert that a current observation governs whether the trigger starts.
candidates.failure_scenario: A pending trigger for head B is recovered while the database still contains an open CONFLICTING snapshot for head A; the existing tests never exercise this state.

candidates.title: The non-factory polling case bypasses the poller
candidates.detail: The non-factory branch inserts a trigger and calls the store consumer directly, so it does not test whether polling a non-factory PR creates a round. A regression in tracking, event generation, or poller consumption for that case would still pass the test.
candidates.suggestion: Exercise a tracked non-factory PR through the same fake GitHub poller path as the other eligibility cases and assert that no conflict round starts.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller erroneously starts a conflict round for a non-factory PR, but the test bypasses the poller and continues to pass.

candidates.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
candidates.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.
candidates.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing paths before storing them or sending them to any external sink, while retaining whatever representation is needed for local conflict resolution.
candidates.failure_scenario: A changed repository contains a conflicting filename that includes a registered token; the token is stored in conflictFiles in the run state.

candidates.title: Disable auto-merge only after validating the delivery grant and PR head
candidates.detail: The new GitHub mutation runs before stored() and assertFactoryBranchPush validate that the grant still holds and that the PR is still open on the expected branch and head. A stale conflict round can therefore change auto-merge settings even when its delivery is subsequently refused.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and recheck state after the mutation before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR head or round grant changes while a conflict round is running and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the stale round.

candidates.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment
candidates.detail: The idempotency check accepts the marker in any PR comment without verifying its author. A PR participant can post the predictable marker before delivery, causing the factory to treat the required resolution summary as already published.
candidates.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

candidates.title: A stale saved snapshot can start a round for a draft PR
candidates.detail: When a saved poller snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. A PR can become draft or close without changing its head, so the saved observation still passes the start checks. Delivery eventually checks draft status, but the forbidden round and its model work have already started.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR state before starting a pending conflict trigger, and leave the trigger pending if its current state cannot be verified.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller saves an open non-draft PR, the owner converts it to draft, and a land conflict trigger is processed before the next poll. A conflict round starts from the stale snapshot.

candidates.title: A stale poller snapshot permanently discards a land conflict trigger
candidates.detail: The request says a landing queue conflict must start a conflict round and that the trigger must survive restart. Whenever any saved PR snapshot exists, this path uses it without refreshing it. If its head predates the approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". The later poll updates the snapshot, but the skipped trigger is never reconsidered, so the blocked entry has no round.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger, or leave a trigger pending when its saved observation is older than the trigger head and retry after a fresh observation.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, then the land queue detects a conflict at B. The saved A snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped permanently.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before verifying the PR and delivery grant
candidates.detail: The new conflict delivery path changes GitHub state before assertFactoryBranchPush validates that the PR is open, still has the authorized head and branch, and still belongs to the expected repository. A stale or invalid round can therefore disable auto-merge on a PR even though its push is subsequently refused. This is an unrequested side effect of a failed delivery.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the asynchronous call before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict round finishes after the PR head has moved and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then refuses the push because the head no longer matches the reviewed SHA.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires "one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA, conflicting file names and resulting SHA, but does not describe how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reviewer cannot learn the resolution from the comment.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, checked description of the actual resolution in the idempotent comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a shared function is resolved and pushed; the PR comment names that file but gives no account of which behavior was retained or changed.

findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the owning run is still delivering, and reconsider it when that run reaches a terminal state.

findings.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
findings.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
findings.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

Startup processing is guarded by “if (!this.conflictStartup)” (src/land/queue.ts:128-135), with no periodic retry. candidates.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the owning run is still delivering, and reconsider it when that run reaches a terminal state.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller observes a newly opened factory PR as CONFLICTING while its owner is still running. The trigger is marked skipped as not a factory PR; the owner subsequently succeeds, but subsequent polls see the same conflicting state and never start a round.

candidates.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
candidates.detail: The request says a landing-queue entry blocked by a conflict starts a conflict round and that the trigger survives restart. If any saved PR snapshot exists, processing uses it without refreshing it. When that snapshot has an older head than the land entry's approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". It is then no longer pending, so a later poll of the correct head cannot recover it.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before deciding eligibility for a land trigger, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can be checked.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved for landing before the next poll, and the land queue finds a base conflict. The trigger records B but is permanently skipped against the saved snapshot of A.

duplicates.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
duplicates.detail: When any saved snapshot exists, the trigger is processed against it without a fresh PR lookup. If the snapshot predates the land entry's approved head, `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped as `PR head moved`. A later poll cannot recover it because the trigger is no longer pending, and a conflicting mergeability episode may already have been observed.
duplicates.suggestion: Obtain a current observation before deciding eligibility for a land trigger, or leave mismatched observations pending until a current observation resolves them.
duplicates.failure_scenario: The poller last saved head A, the PR advances to head B, and the land queue approves B and finds a conflict before the next poll. The trigger for B is permanently skipped against snapshot A.

candidates.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
candidates.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

candidates.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
candidates.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
candidates.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

candidates.title: The non-factory poller case bypasses the poller
candidates.detail: The non-factory branch manually inserts and consumes a trigger instead of running the poller. It verifies the store's refusal but cannot catch a regression in how polling handles a conflicting non-factory PR, despite the test name and the requested poller acceptance case.
candidates.suggestion: Drive a non-factory conflicting PR through the fake GitHub poller and assert that it starts no round.
candidates.failure_scenario: A future change makes the poller start rounds for non-factory observations while the direct store-level setup in this test still passes.

candidates.title: Missing draft state is treated as permission to proceed
candidates.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
candidates.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the current PR head
candidates.detail: The new delivery path changes the PR's auto-merge setting before checking that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected repository and branch, and remains at the reviewed head. A stale round can therefore mutate a PR even though the subsequent delivery guard rejects it.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the stored grant and current PR identity before disabling auto-merge, then revalidate after the awaited mutation and before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR head changes while a conflict round runs and a user enables auto-merge for the new head. The stale round disables auto-merge, then fails its head check without pushing.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires that "The PR gets one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA and conflicted file names, but contains no account of how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reader cannot assess the resolution from it.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, reviewed summary of the actual resolution in the comment, with the existing publication and redaction checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a file is resolved by combining two behavioral changes; the resulting comment names the file and commit but does not explain the combined behavior.

findings.title: Cached first attempts lose the workspace needed by retries after restart
findings.detail: A completed first attempt is reused from state after restart, but the resumed stage cleans the checkout before reaching this line. A pending or newly started retry therefore runs without the build output or other files produced by that first attempt. Previously, a resumed gate stage reran the first attempt and recreated those files before retrying.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the workspace required by a pending retry, or replay the local first attempt before performing the retry after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate setup creates an ignored build directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts before or during its retry. On resume, checkoutCommitted removes the directory, the cached initial result is reused, and the retry fails because its build output is missing.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue))` before resuming gates. src/git/repos.ts:476 runs `git clean -ffdxq`, removing ignored and untracked build output. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 then returns `results[purpose]` for the saved initial attempt, while src/gates/run.ts:280 retries with `{ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected }`.
verification.trigger: Restart after the initial result is persisted but before its regression retry completes. Resume removes setup-generated artifacts, skips the cached initial execution and its setup, and runs the retry without its required artifacts, producing a false failure.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed

Gate reporting and landing logs currently work only because the local executor calls hooks directly; an executor implementing the advertised interface has no way to deliver its streamed check events to those consumers.

Prepare likewise discards changes before resuming its baseline retry.

findings.failure_scenario: A setup or initial check creates an untracked build artifact, a later check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. The resumed retry cannot find the artifact and produces a different verdict.

findings.suggestion: Keep sensitive request data out of the persisted handle and reconstruct the local request from trusted run state when reattaching, without transforming executable input.

findings.title: Cargo home allowance exposes registry credentials to gate commands
findings.detail: The gate profile grants file reads throughout Cargo home, but neither the built-in deny list nor the later specific-deny rules exclude Cargo's credentials or credentials.toml files. This leaves registry tokens accessible to candidate code despite the requirement that credential stores fall outside the gate allowlist.

That collects only recognizable literals and holdout phrases, so an ordinary sentence unique to the verifier is not added to the redaction catalogue. If a report quotes that sentence outside the holdout section, it is returned unchanged, contrary to the requirement to withhold verifier prose and report lines quoting holdout material.
findings.suggestion: Treat verifier notes as private observations when building the catalogue, and add a test with a plain-prose verifier note quoted in a report.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier note says "The violet otter failed again." for a holdout check, and the report repeats that sentence outside the holdout section. If those words are absent from the holdout scenarios and public sources, the report exposes the sentence.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:254 calls `collect(verify?.notes)` without enabling `privateProse`. Whole prose enters the redaction catalogue only when `privateProse` is true (lines 240–244). Otherwise src/pipeline/prompts.ts:247 only runs `collectLiterals(observed)`, whose pattern (lines 231–234) does not match ordinary prose such as `The violet otter failed again.` Reports outside the holdout section pass through this catalogue-based redactor (src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:521–523).
verification.trigger: A verifier's notes contain holdout-only prose with no syntax-shaped literals, absent from the scenarios and public sources. A report repeats it outside the holdout section, and limitless_get_change returns the sentence unwithheld.

findings.title: Hidden test fixture is never quoted in the report
findings.detail: The test writes a hidden test file but places only its sentinel in the report. It therefore verifies redaction of a detail copied into the holdout scenario, but does not verify that a report line quoting hidden test text stays withheld.
findings.suggestion: Add a report line quoting the hidden test text and assert that the line is withheld while an unrelated report line remains visible.
findings.failure_scenario: A report quotes hidden test code containing details absent from the holdout scenario, and the change view returns that quotation.

verification.evidence: test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:180 writes hidden code containing `.toBe('PRIVATE')`, but :187 puts the quoted sentinel in the scenario and :206 reports only `Quoted hidden test: ${hidden}`. Thus the test exercises scenario matching, not hidden-file quotation protection. src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:227 harvests `privateHoldoutDetails(holdout, publicSources)`; :264–299 adds verification records and diagnostics, but never hidden-file contents. At :351–355, report lines are withheld only when catalogue matching succeeds; :521–523 returns the remaining report text.
verification.trigger: A report outside the holdout section quotes hidden-test code whose details occur in neither the scenario nor saved verifier observations—for example, `expect(result).toBe('PRIVATE')`. The quotation passes through because hidden-file contents are absent from the redaction catalogue. The added fixture does not test this case.

findings.title: Diffs quoted in reports still expose multiline credentials
findings.detail: The new line-prefix-aware filter is applied only to the diff field. Reports returned by the same tool still pass through literal privacy matching, so a report containing a unified diff with each credential line prefixed by '+' or '-' exposes the credential. The request explicitly includes other outputs that render diffs or requires them to be listed as follow-ups.
findings.suggestion: Apply equivalent line-prefix-aware credential filtering to diff quotations in reports, or explicitly document this output as a follow-up as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains '+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret' and 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' is registered as a credential; report.text returns both lines.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:652–654 returns reports using `privacy(report) === report ? privacy(withoutHoldoutSection(report, holdoutRedact)) : protect(report)`, without applying `privatePatchLines`. src/gates/private.ts:70 checks `layer.includes(protectedText)`. A probe confirmed zero matches for the registered multiline credential in '+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret', with credential redaction leaving it unchanged.
verification.trigger: A persisted report outside the withheld holdout section contains '+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret'; registering 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' still allows both fragments into report.text.

findings.title: Repeated credential matches make patch filtering quadratic
findings.detail: Every occurrence scans every line range synchronously before paging. An untrusted large patch with many occurrences of a registered multiline value can therefore block the daemon's event loop for a prolonged period, and each page request repeats the work. A targeted invocation of the extracted function took 893 ms for 50,000 lines and 3,514 ms for 100,000 lines, consistent with quadratic growth.
findings.suggestion: Map match offsets to affected ranges using an ordered cursor or binary search, so work grows with the patch size and number of matching lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed file contains hundreds of thousands of repetitions of a two-line registered credential; requesting its change view monopolizes the daemon event loop for minutes.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:80–84 calls `withhold(start, start + literal.length)` for every occurrence; lines 73–76 implement each call with `for (const range of ranges)`. Thus repetitions require quadratic range comparisons before paging. A bounded probe measured roughly 4ms, 27ms and 100ms for 1,000, 4,000 and 8,000 repetitions. src/util/proc.ts:603 allows `SH_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 50_000_000`.
verification.trigger: A patch containing hundreds of thousands of repetitions remains below the output cap but causes billions of synchronous range comparisons, blocking the daemon event loop; sufficiently large inputs can take minutes.

findings.title: Clipped credential matches leave changed lines visible
findings.detail: When a hunk ends partway through a multiline credential, the clipped-prefix match withholds only context lines. The adjacent-pair check does not cover a credential that starts in the middle of a patch line, so a deleted or added line containing that credential fragment remains visible.
findings.suggestion: Map clipped matches to every affected patch line, including additions and deletions, and cover credentials embedded within surrounding line text.
findings.failure_scenario: A ten-line credential starts after a public prefix on a line. Changing that first line produces a hunk containing only the first few credential lines. The old-side prefix matches, but the deleted first line is excluded by the clipped filter and does not match the whole-line pair check, so its credential fragment appears in the patch.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:90–91 calls `withhold(..., true)` for a clipped prefix, but line 75 requires `(!clipped || range.prefix === " ")`. The fallback at lines 101–102 requires `framed.includes(`\n${pair}`)`. A probe with '-key=secret-0' followed by three credential context lines withheld the context but retained '-key=secret-0'.
verification.trigger: A ten-line credential begins after 'key=' on its first line. Replacing that line creates a hunk ending inside the credential; the deleted credential fragment remains visible because clipped matching excludes deletions and the public prefix defeats whole-line pair matching.

findings.title: Review prompts still include unredacted line-prefixed diffs
findings.detail: The request also requires other outputs that render diffs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups. Review prompts include patch text, while the existing literal credential redaction cannot match a multiline credential split by diff prefixes. This path was neither changed nor identified as a follow-up.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same patch-aware credential filtering before diff text is sent to reviewers, or explicitly document this output as the requested follow-up.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change diff adds a file containing a registered two-line credential. The review prompt contains the two lines prefixed with `+`, so literal credential redaction does not remove them before the prompt is sent to a model.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:602 returns `patch: patch.stdout`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1435 passes it into review input: `...(ctx.state.flow === "verify-change" ? { patch: reviewDiff.patch } : {})`. src/pipeline/prompts.ts:398 applies `input = redactGateData(input)`, then :460 embeds `fence(input.patch.slice(0, PATCH_LIMIT) || "(empty diff)")`. That redactor calls `redactCredentials(stripVTControlCharacters(output))` (src/gates/output.ts:23), whose matching is literal: `text = text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")` (src/util/proc.ts:684). The added patch-aware filtering is confined to `getChange` (src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:597); this prompt path does not use it. src/harness/claude.ts:376 sends `stdin: spec.prompt`.
verification.trigger: A verify-change patch contains an added multiline registered credential within the prompt excerpt. Git inserts `+` before each line, preventing literal matching of the registered value; both credential lines reach the review model.

The request explicitly includes diffs rendered in reports and asks for untreated outputs to be listed as follow-ups.
findings.suggestion: Apply line-prefix-aware credential filtering to diffs in reports, or document this output as a follow-up as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A stored report contains consecutive lines '+alpha-secret' and '+beta-secret', while 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' is registered. Requesting its report page returns both credential fragments.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:652–656 pages `privacy(withoutHoldoutSection(report, holdoutRedact))` without reconstructing quoted diff lines. src/gates/private.ts:70 uses `layer.includes(protectedText)`, which cannot match 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' across '\n+'. The direct privacy-matching probe returned zero matches.

findings.suggestion: Add a report-page test with a registered multiline credential split across diff-prefixed lines, checking that neither fragment appears and unrelated report text remains visible.
findings.failure_scenario: A report artifact contains a quoted diff with '+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret' and the registered credential is 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret'; the current test suite does not check the returned report for either fragment.

findings.title: Keep reviewer execution time out of failed-trial preparation timing
findings.detail: The catch path recomputes preparationMs whenever roundsUsed is absent. Review trials never set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts overwrites the already-recorded preparation duration with elapsed time including the reviewer invocation. The reported preparation and trial times are no longer separate for that failure.
findings.suggestion: Record the preparation duration once, and only calculate it in the catch path if preparation did not finish.
findings.failure_scenario: A review invocation runs for several minutes and then throws, for example on an origin-exclusion failure. Its preparationMs includes those minutes even though setup had already completed.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:689-690 records completed preparation: `const preparationMs = Date.now() - preparationStarted; ... trial.details.preparationMs = preparationMs`. Only implement cases set `roundsUsed` (1101-1104). An origin-exclusion error is rethrown at 1073: `if (originFailure) throw originFailure;`. The outer catch overwrites review preparation timing at 1201-1202: `"defects" in item && preparationStarted !== undefined && !trial.details.roundsUsed ? { preparationMs: Date.now() - preparationStarted }`.
verification.trigger: A review runs for minutes after successful setup, then throws an origin-exclusion error. Since review trials never set roundsUsed, the catch replaces preparationMs with elapsed preparation plus reviewer execution time, producing incorrect recorded timing.

findings.title: Setup variants can make routing policy select the wrong trial arm
findings.detail: The request says production is unchanged and gives the setup-enabled standard prompt a separate cache identity. That identity also makes a setup-enabled system and an otherwise identical system valid in the same eval. Policy selection assumes at most one standard system per target, however, and generatePolicy takes only the first summary. It therefore silently ignores one arm, with the selected evidence depending on system ordering.
findings.suggestion: Define which standard arm is eligible for routing policy and update policy selection to handle both configurations explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains standard systems for the same target with and without setup. Both pass configuration validation, but policy generation uses only the first system's results even if the other arm has different outcomes.

verification.evidence: src/evals/cache.ts:49 hashes every configuration field except name: `reviewSystemHash({ name: _name, ...config }: ReviewSystem)`, so setup variants differ and pass the duplicate-hash check in src/evals/cases.ts:426-430. src/evals/policy.ts:133-143 selects standard systems for the target without checking setup, then takes `summarize(...)[0]`. src/evals/stats.ts:320-329 creates separate summaries by system name: `const declared = run.systems?.map((system) => system.name)` and `const rows = trials.filter((t) => candidateOf(t) === candidate)`.
verification.trigger: An eval includes standard single-review systems for one target, differing only in setup and name. Both qualify for policy evidence, but policy generation uses only the first system summary. Different outcomes in the other arm are silently ignored, making routing depend on arm ordering.

findings.title: A reviewer exception is counted as preparation time
findings.detail: The request says the report records trial and preparation time separately. Review trials do not set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts enters this branch and replaces preparationMs with the elapsed time since preparation began, including the reviewer invocation.
findings.suggestion: Track whether preparation completed separately and preserve the recorded preparationMs when a later invocation fails.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the initial TLS connection
findings.detail: The initial connection accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that connection. A man-in-the-middle can relay the pairing request to the real coordinator, return its code and secret to the worker, and present its own certificate. The owner sees the same code on both sides and approves it; the attacker then observes the claim and issued token. Pinning the attacker's certificate on subsequent requests does not prevent this. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never authenticated or used to bind the exchange.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to both endpoints' certificate fingerprints and the pairing exchange, so relaying through a different TLS certificate changes the code or causes verification to fail.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, proxies the real coordinator's pairing response, and forwards the approved claim while terminating both TLS connections.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-27 sends the initial pairing request with only `{ signal }`; src/workers/tls.ts:103 sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`, and :114 checks the certificate only when `options.pin !== undefined`. src/workers/client.ts:39 then pins `first.fingerprint`. src/db/workers.ts:85-93 issues the approved token based solely on the relayed pairing secret.
verification.trigger: An interceptor terminates TLS and relays the coordinator's pairing response and claim. Both endpoints display the same code, but the interceptor learns the approved token and the worker pins the interceptor's certificate.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
findings.detail: Private read protection is an in-memory registry. Pairing releases the token and fingerprint registrations on return, and `runWorker` registers them only in the worker CLI process. A daemon running gates or agents in a separate process therefore does not include those files in its sandbox deny paths. The coordinator TLS key has the same lifetime problem when its listener is disabled after the key has been created. Mode 0600 does not protect files from another process running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register the configured worker credential and TLS key paths in every process that constructs agent or gate sandboxes, independent of whether a worker or listener is currently running.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, then run a factory daemon and a gate on the same machine; the daemon's sandbox is built without the worker token path registered, allowing a gate with access to that path to read the token.

verification.evidence: src/util/private-reads.ts:4 uses a process-local `const privatePaths = new Map<string, number>()`. src/workers/client.ts:47-48 registers the credential files, then :57 calls every release function. src/cli/daemon.ts:15-31 registers the API credential and listener material, but never loads worker credentials. src/harness/read-policy.ts:217 applies the broad gate deny only to `options.home ?? homedir()`.
verification.trigger: Pair a worker and start a separate daemon. Its sandbox deny list lacks the worker credentials. With a supported data directory outside the home and outside other denied roots, a gate can read the same-user token despite its 0600 mode.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently blocks restart
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before invoking OpenSSL. If generation fails, times out, or the process stops before both files are complete, the next start either rejects the incomplete pair or tries to parse invalid material. No cleanup or recovery occurs, so the worker listener or pairing command continues to fail on every subsequent start.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names, validate them, and publish them only after successful generation; clean up incomplete temporary material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating the empty key file but before OpenSSL creates the certificate; every later listener start throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 creates `writeFileSync(keyPath, "", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 })` before awaiting OpenSSL at line 19. Line 17 throws `new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material")` when only one file exists; lines 45–47 only `release(); throw error;`, leaving files intact. src/cli/daemon.ts:30 awaits listener startup before starting the daemon.
verification.trigger: With the worker listener enabled, interruption after key.pem creation but before cert.pem creation leaves persistent incomplete TLS material. Every subsequent daemon startup fails until manual repair.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. The displayed code comes from the coordinator but is not bound to that certificate or to an authenticated exchange. An intermediary can relay the pairing request and code unchanged, obtain the pairing secret and issued token, and leave the worker pinned to the intermediary's certificate even though the owner compared matching codes.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and pairing exchange so a relaying intermediary cannot obtain a usable token or substitute its certificate.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, forwards the request to the real coordinator, and relays its code. The owner approves the matching code; the attacker claims the token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:103 uses `rejectUnauthorized: false`; :114 validates only an explicitly supplied pin. src/workers/client.ts:27 supplies no initial pin, :33 prints the response's code, :39 trusts the first connection's fingerprint, and :47 persists it. src/db/workers.ts:88-93 authenticates token claims using only `pairing_secret_hash`.
verification.trigger: An interceptor forwards pairing to the real coordinator and relays its code. Owner approval authorizes that request, while the interceptor can claim the token and cause the worker to persist the interceptor's certificate fingerprint.

findings.title: Permanent TLS and configuration errors are retried silently forever
findings.detail: The heartbeat loop catches every request exception and retries without a deadline or diagnostic. This includes a changed coordinator fingerprint and malformed coordinator URL, neither of which can be repaired by retrying. The worker remains running but never sends another heartbeat, and the owner receives no explanation.
findings.suggestion: Retry only transient transport failures with a bounded policy; propagate permanent validation and certificate-pin failures with their original reason.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing. Every heartbeat fails fingerprint validation, but the worker silently retries indefinitely instead of reporting that it must be paired again.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a changed certificate with `new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed")`. src/workers/client.ts:99-102 catches every request error and returns `undefined`; :93 loops `for (;;)`, and :106-107 sleeps and retries with delay capped at 10 seconds.
verification.trigger: The coordinator certificate changes, or the coordinator URL is invalid. Every heartbeat throws a permanent validation error, which is silently swallowed and retried indefinitely; the worker remains offline without reporting the required correction.

findings.title: Existing TLS key loses sandbox protection when the listener is disabled
findings.detail: The TLS key is registered with the sandbox deny list only when the listener starts. After a listener has created the key, restarting the daemon with workers.listen unset skips registration even though the key remains on disk. Agent sandboxes that can read that data directory can then read the coordinator's private key, contrary to the requirement that it be denied in every agent sandbox.
findings.suggestion: Register protection for existing worker TLS material independently of whether the listener is enabled, and retain it for the daemon lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the listener once, then disable it and restart the daemon with the data directory outside the default home deny paths. A subsequent agent can read worker-tls/key.pem.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:15–16: `if (!listen) return undefined;` precedes `certificate(join(paths.home, "worker-tls"))`. src/workers/tls.ts:12–14 registers protection only there: `const keyPath = join(home, "key.pem")` and `const release = protectPrivateFile(keyPath);`. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 initializes a process-local registry: `const privatePaths = new Map<string, number>();`. src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 derives sandbox denies from `privateReadPaths()`.
verification.trigger: Enable workers once, then restart with the listener disabled and the data directory outside generic denied paths. The retained TLS key receives no sandbox deny registration and an agent running as the same user can read it despite mode 0600.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents future startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before running openssl, but its error path leaves partial files behind. A timeout, failed openssl invocation, or interruption can therefore leave only the empty key or other incomplete material. Every later start rejects the incomplete material, requiring manual cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them only after successful generation, cleaning up partial temporary files on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is interrupted after creating key.pem but before openssl writes cert.pem. Subsequent starts fail with `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 writes an empty key.pem before `await sh(...)` at line 19. On restart, line 17 throws `"Incomplete worker TLS material"` if key.pem exists without cert.pem. The catch at lines 45–47 releases protection and rethrows without removing the incomplete files. src/cli/daemon.ts:30 propagates listener startup failure.
verification.trigger: Interrupt initial certificate generation after key.pem is created and before cert.pem is written. Subsequent starts with the worker listener enabled cannot start the daemon without manual repair.

findings.title: Credential read protection ends with the pairing process
findings.detail: The worker token and coordinator fingerprint are registered in an in-memory deny list only while `pairWorker` or `runWorker` holds them. Pairing releases both registrations before exiting, and a separately running daemon has its own deny list. Likewise, an existing coordinator TLS key is not registered when the listener is disabled. An agent sandbox created by that daemon therefore does not receive these paths as private-file denies.
findings.suggestion: Register persisted worker credential and TLS-key paths in every process that constructs agent sandbox policies, independently of whether pairing, the worker loop or the listener is currently running.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, exit the pairing command, and run an agent through a separate daemon using the same data directory: that daemon's private-file deny list does not contain the stored worker token or coordinator fingerprint.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:55-57 releases credential protection when pairing finishes. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 stores registrations only in a module-local Map, and :21 deletes released paths. src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 builds denies from `credentials` and `privateReadPaths()`; :217 adds a home-wide deny only for gates, not editors. src/cli/daemon.ts:15-31 never registers existing worker token or fingerprint files.
verification.trigger: After pairing exits, a separate daemon using the same data directory starts an editor agent. The editor's deny list lacks `<data>/worker/token` and `<data>/worker/coordinator-fingerprint`, allowing same-user reads of the stored credentials.

findings.title: Privacy probe masks the cross-process credential protection gap
findings.detail: The real-Seatbelt test creates the TLS material and registers both worker files in the same process that starts the gate, retaining all registrations throughout the probe. It consequently passes even if a daemon started separately after pairing has no credential paths in its in-memory deny list.

findings.failure_scenario: The current implementation releases the registrations after pairing, yet this test retains them and reports all three files denied.

Actual pairing releases those registrations, and registrations held by a separate worker process cannot protect another process's sandboxes. findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that untrusted connection. An active intermediary can forward the request to the real coordinator, relay its code to the worker, and retain the returned pairing secret. The owner and worker see matching codes, but the intermediary can claim the approved token and the worker pins the intermediary's certificate.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes

A separately running daemon on the same machine does not receive those registrations when it constructs Claude or Codex sandbox policies, so its agents can read the persistent worker token and coordinator fingerprint. Mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.

findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a worker and a factory daemon under the same user. An agent launched by the daemon reads `<data>/worker/token` and impersonates that worker.

findings.title: Disabling the listener leaves its existing TLS key unprotected from agents

After an owner removes `workers.listen` and restarts the daemon, the existing key remains on disk but is no longer included in agent sandbox deny paths. An agent running as the same user can read it, compromising the certificate trusted by already paired workers if the listener is later re-enabled.
findings.suggestion: Register the persistent TLS key path independently of whether the listener is currently enabled, or securely remove and rotate the material when disabling it.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator previously enabled workers, then starts with the listener disabled. A tool-enabled agent reads `<data>/worker-tls/key.pem` before the listener is enabled again.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied in the daemon's agent sandboxes
findings.detail: The request requires the worker token and coordinator fingerprint to be read-denied to gates. The deny registry is process-local, but pairing and the worker loop run as separate CLI processes from the daemon. Their registrations are also released when those commands exit. A daemon on the same machine therefore does not add these files to its agent sandbox deny lists; mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.

findings.failure_scenario: A machine is both a paired worker and a coordinator. An agent launched by its daemon reads the token under the worker data directory and uses it to impersonate the worker.
