findings.detail: The request requires a worker that lost its claim to write nothing, but denying the response also leaves the earlier `rerun_requested` record unresolved. The successor only resolves that record when GitHub reports a later workflow attempt; a rejected POST creates no such attempt. The land can consequently wait for CI indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Give the successor a way to reconcile a rerun request that was rejected or never confirmed, without allowing the stale worker to write after losing ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker records `rerun_requested`, another owner reclaims the entry while the POST is in flight, and GitHub returns HTTP 422. The old worker discards the response and subsequent inspections keep waiting for a workflow attempt that never exists.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:2900 records "outcome = 'rerun_requested'". src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:236-237 awaits the POST then calls "allowed();", which throws on claim loss (97-98), preventing the HTTP rejection handler (242-243). Subsequent inspections execute "if (run.run_attempt <= origin.attempt) continue;" (293) and "if (!refused) continue;" for pending records without refusal metadata (438-440).

findings.title: A stale gate callback can append to the replacement worker's log
findings.detail: The request says a worker that lost its claim writes nothing. Gate result callbacks append without checking ownership, and every attempt uses the same log path. A result arriving after reclaim can therefore alter the newer attempt's log, including after the replacement worker has truncated and started writing it.
findings.suggestion: Guard gate log writes against claim loss and isolate log paths by attempt so late callbacks cannot modify the replacement worker's evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate is running when another worker reclaims the entry and starts its checks. Before the old heartbeat detects the loss, the old gate reports a result and appends it to the shared `land-<id>.log`.

findings.title: A rejected rerun can remain pending indefinitely after reclaim
findings.detail: The rerun is recorded as rerun_requested before the POST. If the land claim changes while that POST is pending, the new guard discards even a definitive rejection response. Subsequent inspections only resolve that pending record when GitHub reports a later workflow attempt, which a rejected POST will never create. The replacement worker therefore waits until its CI deadline instead of reporting the failure; polling also keeps the failure pending.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable reconciliation path for a rerun whose response was lost to a claim change, including definitive rejection, without letting the stale worker write after losing ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient CI failure triggers a rerun POST, another worker reclaims the land entry while the request is pending, and GitHub returns HTTP 422. The record remains rerun_requested with no later attempt, so the replacement cannot finish CI classification.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:2900 persists `outcome = 'rerun_requested'` before the POST. src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:236-243 does `const res = await call(...)`, then `allowed()`, before handling HTTP 4xx with `reject(...)`. Lines 97-98 throw when ownership is lost. Replacement inspections skip unchanged attempts at line 293 (`if (run.run_attempt <= origin.attempt) continue`) and skip pending failures without a recorded refusal at lines 438-440 (`if (!refused) continue`).
verification.trigger: Reclaim the land entry while its rerun POST is pending, then return HTTP 422 without starting another workflow attempt. The ownership guard discards the refusal; the durable rerun_requested record remains unresolved, preventing the replacement from completing CI classification.

findings.title: A lost claim can leave a refused CI rerun permanently pending
findings.detail: The rerun is recorded as rerun_requested before the POST. If the land claim is reclaimed while the POST is in flight, the new guard discards its response. When GitHub refused the request, no later workflow attempt exists to resolve the pending record, and subsequent inspections keep waiting for one. The replacement land eventually blocks on its CI timeout, and the pending CI failure remains unresolved.
findings.suggestion: Provide a guarded reconciliation path for an in-flight rerun response so the current owner can record a refusal without letting the stale worker write.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient CI failure triggers a rerun POST; another worker reclaims the land entry before GitHub returns HTTP 422. The old worker discards the refusal, leaving rerun_requested even though no rerun was started.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:236-243 checks `allowed()` immediately after the rerun POST resolves and before `reject(f, excerpt)`. Lines 541-548 convert denied writes into a pending decision. src/db/store.ts:2900 already persisted `outcome = 'rerun_requested'`; subsequent inspections require a later workflow attempt (ci-classifier.ts:293) and otherwise skip the pending record (lines 438-440).
verification.trigger: A new worker reclaims ownership before GitHub returns HTTP 422 for the old worker's rerun POST. No rerun starts, but the refusal is discarded and subsequent inspections leave the failure permanently pending for that unchanged head and workflow attempt.

findings.title: A stale gate can still write into the replacement worker's log
findings.detail: Worktrees now have attempt-specific paths, but gate logs still use one path per land entry. The gate result callback appends without checking ownership. After reclaim, the replacement can truncate or write that same log while the old gate is still running; a late old result then contaminates the replacement's log. This also violates the request that a worker which lost its claim write nothing.
findings.suggestion: Use attempt-specific log paths and prevent stale gate callbacks from writing after claim loss.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A is awaiting a gate when worker B reclaims the entry and starts its own checks. A's gate finishes before its next heartbeat and appends its output to B's land log.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:435 uses the shared path `land-${entry.id}.log`; src/land/queue.ts:454–458 defines `onResult: (r: GateResult) => appendFileSync(log, ...)` without checking ownership. src/gates/executor.ts:217 invokes `hooks.onResult?.(...)` before executeGate returns; the ownership check occurs afterward at src/land/queue.ts:462.
verification.trigger: B reclaims the entry and initializes its log while A awaits a gate. A's result arrives before its heartbeat detects reclaim and appends stale output to B's log.

findings.title: Cover claim loss while a land gate is running
findings.detail: The new tests cover deferred merge, CI, push, and lookup responses, but none reclaims the entry while `executeGate` is pending. The new ownership checks around the gate's log-path and flaky-result writes therefore have no regression test.
findings.suggestion: Defer a gate result, reclaim the entry, then release the result and assert that the replacement claim, log path, reason, and events remain unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker loses its claim while a gate is running; if the ownership guard after the gate regresses, its late result can write a log path or outcome onto the replacement worker's entry.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:460–462: `const run = await executeGate(...)`; `signal.throwIfAborted();`; `this.owned(entry.id, () => this.store.updateLandEntry(entry.id, { logPath: log }));`. This guard exists but lacks a gate-time reclaim test. test/land-queue.test.ts:1576 stops the worker with `await first.stop()` before restarting; the reclaim test at :3024 instead defers `checkPrivatePublication`, after the stale worker's gates have completed.
verification.trigger: Reclaim an entry while its gate is pending, then release the gate before the next heartbeat. No existing test checks that the replacement entry remains unchanged at this boundary, so a regression of the post-gate ownership guard could go undetected. This is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated production failure at HEAD.

findings.title: A reclaimed worker can still write to the shared gate log
findings.detail: Gate result callbacks append to a log named only by entry ID without checking claim ownership. A replacement attempt uses the same log path and truncates it when its checks start, so a delayed callback from the old worker can append stale results to the replacement's log after the claim was reclaimed. This violates the requested guarantee that a worker which lost its claim writes nothing and can misrepresent the checks for the current attempt.
findings.suggestion: Use attempt-specific log paths and ensure callbacks stop writing once the claim is lost.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A is waiting for a gate result when worker B reclaims the entry and starts its checks. Before A's next heartbeat, A's gate callback appends its result to the same `land-<id>.log` that B is using.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:435 names the log `land-${entry.id}.log`, without an attempt suffix. src/land/queue.ts:441 initializes it with `writeFileSync(log, ...)`, while src/land/queue.ts:454–458 unconditionally calls `appendFileSync(log, ...)` from the result callback.
verification.trigger: After B reclaims the entry and starts checks, A's pending gate emits a result before A's next heartbeat. Both workers use the same log, so A contaminates B's diagnostics.

findings.title: A reclaimed worker can still write to the shared gate log
findings.detail: The request says that a worker that lost its claim writes nothing. Gate result callbacks append to a log shared by all attempts without checking ownership. A replacement worker can start its checks and write the same log while an old gate is still completing, so the old result can be mixed into the replacement attempt's evidence.
findings.suggestion: Guard gate log writes against claim loss and isolate each attempt's log so an already-running callback cannot contaminate the replacement's output.
findings.failure_scenario: Reclaim an entry while its old worker is awaiting executeGate, start checks for the new claim, then release the old gate result before the old heartbeat fires.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:217 forwards check events through `hooks.onResult?.(redactGateData(event.result), event.phase)`. The callback at src/land/queue.ts:454–458 performs `appendFileSync(log, ...)`; `this.owned(...)` at src/land/queue.ts:462 runs only after `await executeGate(...)`.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while A awaits executeGate, start B's checks, then release A's gate result before its heartbeat. A appends output to the shared replacement log before ownership is validated.

findings.title: Checkout retry can continue after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: The request requires confirming ownership after every await before a side effect. If addDetachedWorktree fails after a reclaim, the retry path checks only the abort signal, which may not yet have been aborted by the heartbeat. It then prunes worktrees and starts another checkout despite no longer owning the claim.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership before pruning and again after that await before retrying the checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: Reclaim an entry while its initial addDetachedWorktree is pending, then let that operation fail before the old worker's next heartbeat.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:847 checks `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` before the initial await. Its catch at src/land/queue.ts:852–855 checks only `signal.throwIfAborted()`, then runs `await cacheGit(["git", "worktree", "prune"], ...)` and `await addDetachedWorktree(cache, sha, path, signal)` without rechecking ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while the initial addDetachedWorktree is pending, then reject it before A's heartbeat. A's signal remains active, so it prunes the cache and retries checkout despite losing the claim, performing unnecessary local work.

Verifier: 14 candidates, 14 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: PR numbers cannot target unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number or URL, but the unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A valid number that has no matching factory run is rejected as "run not found", even when its repository is configured.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets in the configured repository context, and report ambiguity when the repository cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183-184: `const run = this.store.getRun(input.target) ?? this.store.runForPr(this.prRef(input.target)); if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);` src/land/queue.ts:226-227: `const match = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/.exec(input.target); if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`
verification.trigger: Request land for bare PR number `7` with its full current SHA and no owning factory run -> the URL-only matcher rejects it with `run not found`.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.
findings.suggestion: Support the head repository when fetching and updating the approved branch, while retaining the pinned-head and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251-252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(`pull request is ${pr.state}`); if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`
verification.trigger: An open fork PR targets a configured repository and supplies its exact current SHA -> it is categorically refused instead of entering the requested land pipeline.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 persists an unowned entry as `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/db/store.ts:100 reads `run_id AS runId`; :2784–2785 claims queued or expired active entries, including `waiting_ci`. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 executes `const run = this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` and `if (!run) throw new Error(`run ${entry.runId} is gone`)`. Its catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, and :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`. HEAD src/core/types.ts:464 excludes blocked entries from active states.
verification.trigger: Rollback to the base release while an unowned land is queued or waiting for CI. Once its claim is available, the older daemon claims it, cannot find run "", and durably blocks it with "run  is gone". Upgrading again does not automatically resume that entry.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:184: `if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);` src/land/queue.ts:226-227: `const match = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/.exec(input.target); if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`
verification.trigger: Request `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` without an owning factory run -> the bare number fails the required URL match and returns `run not found`.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:252: `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`
verification.trigger: An open contributor fork PR targeting a configured repository is requested with its exact current SHA -> the cross-repository guard rejects it.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back; the previous daemon claims it, looks up run `""`, and marks the entry blocked because the run is gone.

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 writes `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/db/store.ts:100 exposes that value through `run_id AS runId`; :2784–2785 permits claiming `waiting_ci` entries after claim expiry. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 looks up that run and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone` when absent. The catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, which persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)` at :912.
verification.trigger: An unowned land awaits CI when deployment rolls back. The previous daemon claims the released or expired entry, looks up run "", and changes the entry to terminal blocked state instead of completing it.

findings.title: Blocked unowned lands disappear from the CLI digest
findings.detail: The new feed entries have a null run ID, but the digest removes every feed item without a run ID before checking whether a blocked land is actionable. Operators relying on the digest therefore do not see these failures, despite the land feed containing them.
findings.suggestion: Teach the digest to resolve unowned land entries by PR URL or land ID and display their current blocked state.
findings.failure_scenario: A confined check fails for an unowned PR; its `land.blocked` feed item exists, but `limitless digest` omits it from blocked lands.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:260 creates unowned entries with `runId: null`. src/db/store.ts:2854 preserves `runId: entry.runId` in feed items. src/cli/digest.ts:62-63 includes `label: "Blocked lands", kinds: ["land.blocked"]`, but src/cli/digest.ts:89-91 then executes `if (!item.runId) { group.items.delete(key); continue; }`.
verification.trigger: An unowned land becomes blocked after a confined check failure -> its feed item has a null runId and the digest deletes it, omitting the blocked land.

findings.title: Unowned pull requests cannot be requested by number
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the existing land command accepts pull request numbers and the request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`. A valid unowned PR supplied as `77` or `#77` is rejected as `run not found`. The new test at test/land-queue.test.ts:2502 asserts that rejection rather than covering acceptance.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a pull request number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, with a clear error when the repository is ambiguous, and test both supported number forms.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured repository has an open, unowned PR 77 and the user runs `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>`; the request fails before querying GitHub.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 passes the argument unchanged: `body: JSON.stringify({ target: sub, ...(values.sha ? { sha: values.sha } : {}) })`. src/land/queue.ts:184 routes missing runs to `requestUnowned(input)`, whose lines 226–227 require a GitHub URL and otherwise execute `if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`.
verification.trigger: An open unowned PR 77 exists on a configured repository; `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` fails with `run not found` before querying GitHub.

findings.title: The unowned land test does not verify actual confinement
findings.detail: The test named as a confined land uses `recordingConfinement`, whose wrapper returns the command unchanged and whose verification only records a call. It therefore passes even if the gate command can write outside its allowed roots. This leaves the request's central confined-check behavior untested for an unowned entry.
findings.suggestion: Add a real Seatbelt integration case, skipped with the existing platform reason where unavailable, that verifies both an allowed checkout write and a denied outside write during an unowned land.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land runs its base check without an effective sandbox, but the recording backend still records verification and the test passes.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:299 injects `confinement: landConfinement.backend`; line 3241 only asserts `expect(landConfinement.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. test/confinement.ts:8–11 implements that backend as `verify: async (roots, opts) => { calls.push({ roots, opts }); }, wrap: (cmd) => cmd`, so it records verification without applying confinement.
verification.trigger: The unowned land test runs checks through a recording backend that leaves commands unchanged. Checks execute without an effective sandbox, yet the confinement assertion passes.

findings.title: Revalidate the PR base before landing
findings.detail: The unowned request snapshots the PR's base branch, but the subsequent land and merge paths do not verify that GitHub still targets that branch. GitHub can change a PR's base without changing its head SHA, so the pinned-head check does not detect a retarget. The queue can run checks from one base and then squash-merge into another, violating the requirement that the destination base's checks govern the land.
findings.suggestion: Re-read and validate the PR's base branch before the merge, and block if it differs from the branch used for the base merge and checks. Ensure the validation is tied as closely as possible to the merge operation.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator approves an unowned PR targeting main. While its land waits for CI, someone retargets it to a release branch without changing its head. The queue checks main's configuration and GitHub merges the approved head into the release branch.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:264 persists `baseBranch: pr.baseRefName`; line 430 later uses `fetchBase(this.deps.paths, repo, entry.baseBranch, signal)`. The final merge inspection at src/git/repos.ts:1463 requests only `"title,body,headRefOid,state"`; lines 1476–1478 invoke `gh pr merge` with `--match-head-commit` but no validation of the PR base.
verification.trigger: After approval and checks against main, someone retargets the PR to a release branch while CI is pending, preserving its head SHA. The merge accepts that SHA and lands into the new branch without checking that branch's base configuration.

findings.title: Accept a PR number for an unowned land
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL. The CLI documents its target as a run, PR number, or URL, and the request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`. An unowned PR supplied as a number always fails with `run not found` even when it belongs to a configured repository.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR-number target against the configured repository context, and return a clear ambiguity error if it cannot be resolved uniquely.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured repository has an open hand-made PR 123. Running `limitless land 123 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183–184: `const run = this.store.getRun(input.target) ?? this.store.runForPr(this.prRef(input.target)); if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);`. Lines 226–227 match only a full GitHub pull-request URL and throw `"run not found"` for a bare number.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 123 --sha <current-full-sha>` targets an open hand-made PR without an owning run; the numeric target is rejected instead of queued.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are excluded from the requested feature
findings.detail: The request says an open PR on a configured GitHub repository that no factory run opened is accepted. This rejects every cross-repository PR, even when its base repository is configured and its head SHA is explicitly approved. Hand-made contributions from forks therefore cannot use the confined land queue.
findings.suggestion: Support fetching and safely pinning fork heads, or explicitly narrow the accepted PR scope.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from their fork against a configured repository and requests landing with its full current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251–252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(...)`; `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. The fork rejection occurs even after the target repository passes the configured-repository check at lines 228–230.
verification.trigger: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository, and landing is requested using its full URL and current full head SHA. The request is refused solely because it originates from a fork, excluding otherwise eligible PRs from the requested feature.

findings.title: Unowned PRs cannot be requested by PR number
findings.detail: The request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, and the existing command accepts PR numbers as well as URLs. The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, so a PR number that has no factory run is rejected as "run not found".
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number against the appropriate configured repository, with a clear error when the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an unowned PR on the configured repository fails before looking up the PR.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:184 delegates unowned targets to `requestUnowned(input)`. Lines 226–227 apply `/^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/` to `input.target` and throw `"run not found"` when it does not match.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` targets an unowned PR on a configured repository; the bare number fails URL validation before any GitHub lookup.

findings.title: Rollback permanently blocks an in-flight runless land
findings.detail: The request requires compatibility with the previous release. A runless entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release resumes active entries by looking up that ID and blocks the entry when no run exists. If a deployment rolls back while such a land is queued or in progress, the old daemon changes it to blocked instead of preserving it for the newer release to resume.
findings.suggestion: Make runless entries invisible to the previous release's active queue, or otherwise provide a rollback-compatible persistence and resume mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: A runless land is waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release; on startup the old queue claims it and blocks it with "run  is gone".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 stores runless entries using `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries; base src/db/store.ts:2784–2785 includes `waiting_ci` in claimable states. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 performs `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` and throws when no run exists. Its error path at :327 and :912 persists the entry as `blocked`; HEAD src/core/types.ts:464 does not include blocked entries in `ACTIVE_LAND_STATES`.
verification.trigger: Rollback while a runless land is waiting for CI. After release or expiry of its claim, the old queue processes it and permanently stops automatic progress with "run  is gone", including after the newer daemon returns.

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:541-547 combines calls using `costUsd: sum((r) => r.costUsd)` and summed usage. src/evals/runner.ts:1139-1144 adds that result to trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:269-275 emits one record with `provider: details.provider`, `modelId: String(t.model_id)` and the entire trial cost; src/db/stats.ts:182 counts `invocations: rows.length`.
verification.trigger: A review eval invokes primary provider A and verifier provider B. Their combined usage and spend become one trial record attributed to A; B receives no separate record.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 stores `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `trial.details.cacheWriteTokens`. src/evals/runner.ts:1173-1175 adds round evidence whenever `"hidden" in item`, including single-round implementation trials. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 then sets both metrics to null when `rounds?.length` is present.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation trial records cache-read 100 and cache-write 20. Because it has round evidence, its model and provider cache totals become null.

findings.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
findings.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1111-1115 selects the verifier target and calls `sendTo(request, to, ...)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:541-547 combines call costs and tokens. src/db/stats.ts:265-275 uses either stored rounds or one fallback record carrying `provider: details.provider` and the complete trial totals, without separate verifier attribution.
verification.trigger: A panel calls reviewer A and verifier B. The statistics assign their combined cost and tokens to A and omit B. For review panels this occurs through the trial fallback record, rather than a stored implementation-round record.

findings.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 accumulates cache splits in trial details across calls. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 explicitly discards them for recorded rounds: `const read = rounds?.length ? null : (details.cacheReadTokens ?? null)` and the equivalent write expression. src/db/stats.ts:291 makes `inputTokens` null when either split is null; src/db/stats.ts:173-175 propagates null through sums.
verification.trigger: A completed multi-round eval has persisted cache totals. Its round records discard those totals, so the eval aggregates return null for cache-read, cache-write and uncached input tokens.

findings.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
findings.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
findings.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:931 persists `store.recordEvalTrial({ ...trial, status: "running" })` before invoking the harness. src/db/stats.ts:246 selects `t.status != 'queued'`; its exclusion at :258 applies only to `t.status === "skipped" || details.preparationFailed`. At :271 it uses `details.invocationStatus ?? String(t.status)`, and :179-180 counts the row while treating only `"ok"` as successful.
verification.trigger: A first-round trial persisted as running before its model call finishes, with no rounds or invocationStatus and zero usage, contributes one unsuccessful eval invocation. Workspace preparation itself precedes this running checkpoint.

findings.title: Eval successful share can reflect grading failures instead of provider results
findings.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and aggregate the provider invocation status separately from the grading outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully, but its grading process times out. The eval provider statistics count the invocation as unsuccessful.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1209-1212 sets `roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason` when the provider returned `"ok"` but grading reports error or timeout. src/db/stats.ts:265-266 selects recorded rounds, :287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 computes success from `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: An implementation invocation succeeds but grading times out or errors; its recorded round is counted as an unsuccessful provider execution.

findings.title: Eval aggregation tests do not exercise runner-produced round evidence
findings.detail: The eval test constructs round records directly and assumes their status and duration describe provider calls. The runner can modify round status after grading and records duration through grading, so this fixture does not catch the resulting misclassification of provider success.
findings.suggestion: Add a test using runner-produced eval evidence where the provider succeeds but grading fails or times out, and assert the provider success share.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression or existing defect that treats a grading timeout as a failed provider invocation passes the manually seeded round test.

verification.evidence: test/provider-workload.test.ts:465-482 manually constructs rounds with `status: "ok"` and `status: "timeout"`, without running the eval runner. src/evals/runner.ts:1208-1212 changes a successful invocation's round status when grading fails: `if (result.status === "ok" && (grade?.implement?.reason === "error" || grade?.implement?.reason === "timeout")) roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason;`. src/db/stats.ts:265-287 consumes those rounds using `status: r.status`; line 180 counts successes only when `r.status === "ok"`.

findings.title: Historical workload omits stored concierge calls
findings.detail: The request asks for long-term provider workload numbers computed from stored invocations. Consequently the new long-term provider and model totals omit that work even when a provider appears in the legacy today and seven-day fields.
findings.suggestion: Include stored chat calls in the historical workload with an appropriate role and their stored model, status, usage, cost, and duration.

findings.suggestion: Count individual calls when evidence supports it, or expose round counts separately without presenting them as invocation counts or invocation success rates.

findings.title: Missing durations are reported as zero total wall time

findings.title: Cross-origin requests can trigger unbounded historical aggregation
findings.detail: The existing GET endpoint now synchronously loads and aggregates every stored invocation and eval trial when no cutoff is supplied. GET requests are exempt from the origin check, so a web page can repeatedly trigger this work against a local daemon even though it cannot read the response. As history grows, each request consumes increasing CPU and memory and blocks the daemon's event loop.
findings.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A user with a large invocation history visits a page that repeatedly loads the local /api/stats/providers URL; each request runs the full historical aggregation and can make the daemon unresponsive.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:385 defaults enforcement off: `requireApiToken: server.require_api_token === true`. src/server/http.ts:225-229 applies the origin guard only when `req.method !== "GET" && req.method !== "HEAD"`. src/server/http.ts:754-756 calls `computeProviderStatistics(store, since === null ? undefined : parseSince(since))` on each request. src/db/stats.ts:232 defaults `since = -8_640_000_000_000_000`; lines 241-248 synchronously load matching invocations and eval trials with `.all(since)`, without a limit.
verification.trigger: With default token enforcement disabled, a browser that permits requests to loopback can repeatedly send cross-origin GETs without since, causing synchronous aggregation of the entire stored history. A sufficiently large history could starve daemon work; the history size and request rate needed for unresponsiveness are not established.

findings.title: A dirty worktree can bypass detection of a cancelled worker's push
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs the local session even if the cancelled worker already pushed an unreported commit. The request requires that case to end NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Check the cancelled job's remote branch for an unreported push before falling back to local execution, including when preparation cannot proceed because the worktree is dirty.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W but has not reported it; after restart the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the leased job, prepare() returns null, and a local session starts instead of reporting the unaccepted push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1138-1139 requires HEAD to match and `(await clean())` for resume. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 then executes `workers.cancelAgentJob(id)` and `id = undefined`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1149 returns `null` on a dirty worktree (`if (!(await clean())) return null;`) before checking the remote at :1150-1155. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:110 executes `if (!prepared) return fallback();`, whose definition at :51 calls `local()` when not aborted.
verification.trigger: A handled worker job has pushed W without an accepted report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty on restart. Reconciliation cancels the job, then prepare returns null before inspecting the remote. A local implementation session starts instead of stopping NeedsHuman for the unaccepted push.

findings.title: A fenced pending report no longer renews its lease
findings.detail: The new result request survives the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller and heldJobs() consequently omits the job from heartbeats. Those heartbeats no longer renew its lease. If result requests remain unavailable while heartbeat requests succeed, the lease expires despite the worker continuing to retry the accepted-report request, and the coordinator rejects the eventual report.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed job in the heartbeat's held-job list while its independently bounded result report is pending, until the result is accepted or the lease is explicitly lost.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during an outage and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result requests fail transiently for longer than the remaining lease or restart grace. The coordinator expires the job; a later result receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:501-504: `heldJobs()` filters on `job.reported && !job.controller.signal.aborted`; the fence aborts those controllers at :565-567. The pushed result nevertheless retries using `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` at :857-862. src/db/workers.ts:242-252 renews leases only for IDs in `c.jobs`, and :415-420 expires an unrenewed lease. src/server/workers.ts:202-203 rejects results with `409` when the lease is no longer held.
verification.trigger: A pushed job's fence fires during coordinator downtime. After restart, successful heartbeats omit that job because its controller remains aborted. If result requests keep failing beyond restart grace, its lease expires despite the live worker; the eventual report receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

findings.title: Late result retries can prevent worker shutdown
findings.detail: The late-result signal excludes the worker's shutdown signal as well as the job cancellation and fence signals. If the coordinator is unreachable, `call()` keeps retrying until the attempt deadline, while `runWorker` waits for every job task in its shutdown cleanup. Stopping the worker can therefore hang for the remainder of the agent attempt, potentially many minutes.
findings.suggestion: Combine the attempt-deadline signal with the worker's shutdown signal while continuing to exclude the job controller used by cancellation and the fence.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit, begins retrying its result during a coordinator outage, and then receives a shutdown signal. Its result request remains active and `runWorker` does not finish until the attempt deadline expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:857-862 sends a pushed result with only `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))`. The retry loop at :507-525 checks and sleeps using that signal. Shutdown at :984-990 calls `stop.abort()`, aborts job controllers, then awaits `...allJobs().map(([, j]) => j.task)`. src/cli/main.ts:383-384 maps SIGINT/SIGTERM to the worker's outer abort controller, which the result signal excludes.
verification.trigger: A worker has pushed and is retrying its report during a coordinator outage when SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives. Shutdown aborts heartbeat and job signals but leaves the report retry active, so runWorker waits until reporting succeeds or the attempt deadline expires.

findings.title: Queued restart test completes the job before the scheduler resumes
findings.detail: The queued case leases and reports the job before calling resumed.start(), so the resumed executor sees a done job. It does not exercise reattachment to a queued job followed by pickup and completion after restart.
findings.suggestion: Start the resumed factory while the job is still queued, observe reattachment, then lease and complete that same ID and assert that no second row is created.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that replaces a stored queued job on resume could pass this integration case because the stored job has already become done.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:940 leases the old job; :943 then awaits `report(resumed, job, request(job), await publish(bare, request(job)))`; only afterward does :945 call `resumed.start()`.
verification.trigger: In the queued restart integration case, the stored job is already done when the scheduler resumes. A regression specific to replacing queued jobs during pipeline resume could pass this case.

findings.title: Already-adopted recovery lacks negative verification cases
findings.detail: The checkpoint test exercises recovery with a valid commit and clean worktree, but does not verify that the new HEAD-already-at-result path rejects a dirty worktree or a commit that fails the shared commit-object checks. Existing adoptWorkerCommit tests exercise the ordinary adoption path.
findings.suggestion: Add recovery cases with HEAD already at the reported SHA and either a dirty worktree or an invalid commit shape, and assert that recovery refuses adoption.
findings.failure_scenario: Removing the cleanliness or commit verification from the already-moved path would still allow the new successful recovery test to pass.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:488 asserts `headSha(state.worktreePath)` equals `first.result_sha`, then :497-498 starts recovery and expects success without introducing dirty files or invalid commit data. The separate protections are at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1201 (`await verifyWorkerCommit(...)`) and :1202 (`... || !(await clean())`). Existing negative tests in test/adopt-worker-commit.test.ts:170 exercise `adopt()`, not this engine recovery branch.
verification.trigger: Removing verification or cleanliness checks specifically from the already-moved recovery branch would leave the successful recovery test passing. Negative tests do not exercise those protections on that branch.

findings.title: Late-report coverage does not test the attempt deadline
findings.detail: The pushed and fenced cases verify that a report survives a restart and fence, but neither holds the coordinator offline until the attempt deadline. The new independent report signal must also stop retrying at that deadline.
findings.suggestion: Add a controlled deadline case that keeps result delivery unavailable through expiry and checks that retries terminate without an accepted result.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression using an unbounded signal for pushed results would still pass the current restart cases and could leave a worker retrying indefinitely.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:774 covers `['running', 'pushed', 'fenced']`; :850-853 waits for publication and optionally fires the fence, then :870 restores connectivity with `offline = false`. It never expires the attempt deadline. The untested bound is src/workers/client.ts:861: `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))`.
verification.trigger: Replacing the pushed-result timeout signal with an unbounded signal would still pass these restart cases because connectivity returns before the deadline. They do not verify that reporting stops when the attempt deadline expires.

findings.title: Restart grace expires after heartbeat freshness, before one lease period
findings.detail: The request says “a worker that stays unreachable for one lease period after the restart is retried on another worker.” Although the lease-expiry calculation grants 60 seconds, this freshness check fails the job after 30 seconds without a heartbeat. That can discard a worker’s pushed result before the promised lease period has elapsed. The requested freshness formula also specifies this 30-second behavior, so the requirements conflict and need to be reconciled.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the conflicting requirements and make the retry timing and documentation agree; add a test covering an unreachable worker between the freshness and lease deadlines.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes while the coordinator is down and remains unreachable for 31 seconds after restart. The next sweep fails its job as disconnected, even though the 60-second restart lease grace has not elapsed; a subsequent result is rejected.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:104-105 sets `fresh: 30_000` and `lease: 60_000`. src/db/workers.ts:415-425 extends lease expiry using `resumedAt + this.times.lease`, but independently fails freshness when `now - Math.max(w.last_heartbeat_at ?? 0, this.resumedAt ?? Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY) > this.times.fresh`, calling `failAgentJob(j.id, "Worker disconnected")`. That transition clears the worker and lease (src/db/workers.ts:385-389). Result acceptance calls `holdsAgentJob`, which sweeps first (src/db/workers.ts:346-349), and rejects a lost lease with HTTP 409 (src/server/workers.ts:200-206).
verification.trigger: An approved worker has a leased job, a pre-restart heartbeat, and an unexpired attempt deadline. It remains unreachable until 31 seconds after restart. A sweep then revokes its attempt despite the 60-second lease grace; its subsequent pushed-result report is rejected, losing the accepted report needed for adoption.

candidates.suggestion: Add a controlled deadline case that keeps result delivery unavailable through expiry and checks that retries terminate without an accepted result.
candidates.failure_scenario: A regression using an unbounded signal for pushed results would still pass the current restart cases and could leave a worker retrying indefinitely.

candidates.title: Restart grace expires after heartbeat freshness, before one lease period
candidates.detail: The request says “a worker that stays unreachable for one lease period after the restart is retried on another worker.” Although the lease-expiry calculation grants 60 seconds, this freshness check fails the job after 30 seconds without a heartbeat. That can discard a worker’s pushed result before the promised lease period has elapsed. The requested freshness formula also specifies this 30-second behavior, so the requirements conflict and need to be reconciled.
candidates.suggestion: Resolve the conflicting requirements and make the retry timing and documentation agree; add a test covering an unreachable worker between the freshness and lease deadlines.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker pushes while the coordinator is down and remains unreachable for 31 seconds after restart. The next sweep fails its job as disconnected, even though the 60-second restart lease grace has not elapsed; a subsequent result is rejected.

findings.detail: The independent signal allows the result request to continue after the fence aborts the job controller, but heldJobs() excludes jobs whose controller is aborted. The pushed commit then has no accepted report and the run ends NeedsHuman.

findings.title: Cancel the open job when reconciliation fails
findings.detail: If `publication.resume()` throws, the error is propagated while the queued or leased job remains open. The engine can then finish the run as NeedsHuman, but the worker continues executing and can push after the coordinator has stopped waiting for its report. Orphan cleanup only runs at factory start or stop, so it does not close this window.
findings.suggestion: After re-reading the job and handling a concurrently completed result, conditionally cancel an open job before propagating the reconciliation error.
findings.failure_scenario: A resumed leased job is still running when the coordinator's git status command or private-strings read fails. Reconciliation throws, the run ends NeedsHuman, and the worker later pushes a commit.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1143-1144: `catch (error) { throw new NeedsHumanError(...) }`. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:76-79: `if (spec.signal.aborted) return cancelled(id); if (workers.agentJob(id)?.state === "done") continue; throw error;` rethrows without cancelling the open job. src/pipeline/engine.ts:448-449 records the run as `needs_human` without cancelling it.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back after reconciliation
findings.detail: A failed resume check cancels the old job and goes straight to `prepare()`. If the worktree is dirty, or the remote lookup fails, `prepare()` returns null and the executor runs locally without checking whether the cancelled worker already pushed. The existing failed-job path checks the remote before local fallback; this new path bypasses that protection and can continue a run with an unaccepted worker commit on its branch.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an unreconciled job, verify the branch against the stored request before permitting a local fallback; treat an unavailable remote check as an unresolved failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes but its report has not been accepted. After restart, the coordinator worktree is dirty, so resume fails, the job is cancelled, prepare returns null, and a local session runs instead of stopping for the unreported push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 cancels the open job and clears `id`; lines 97-110 then call `publication.prepare()` and `if (!prepared) return fallback()`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1148-1150: `const parentSha = await headSha(cwd); if (!(await clean())) return null; const remote = await remoteSha();`. The dirty-worktree return precedes the remote check. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:51 defines fallback as `spec.signal.aborted ? cancelled(id) : local()`.
verification.trigger: A resumed worker has pushed without an accepted report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the job, preparation returns null before checking the remote, and a local session runs instead of stopping for the unreported push.

findings.title: Queued restart test finishes the job before the coordinator starts
findings.detail: The queued checkpoint case leases and reports the job before calling resumed.start(), so the resumed executor encounters a done job rather than re-attaching to a queued or leased job. The executor-level test covers queued reconciliation in isolation, but this integration case would still pass if a restarted factory could not re-attach to an open queued job.

findings.title: Keep explicitly local panel finders on the coordinator
findings.detail: The shared review call supplies checkout metadata to every production panel finder, while worker eligibility has no indication that a finder was configured as local. The `free_only` routing constraint does not guarantee an ineligible target: the provider configuration accepts a free `claude-cli` or `codex-cli` provider without a backend. Such a finder is dispatched to a worker, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Pass the finder's local designation through the call seam and exclude it from worker eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel finder has `local: true`, routing selects a free `codex-cli` provider, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running on the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 sets only `...(finder?.local ? { billing: "free_only" as const } : {})`, then line 1864 calls the shared `call`. That call supplies `checkout` for GitHub repositories at lines 1840–1843. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 accepts readonly review calls with checkout and a Claude/Codex target without backend credentials; it has no local-finder exclusion. src/router/config-catalog.ts:57–59 permits both `kind: "codex-cli"` and `billing: "free"`.
verification.trigger: With review workers enabled for the GitHub repository, a local finder routed to a free Codex CLI target receives checkout metadata and dispatches to a worker instead of the coordinator.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Eligibility does not identify local finders; it assumes their targets always have backend, openai, or decisions fields. The catalog also permits a free claude-cli or codex-cli provider without those fields, so a local finder routed to such a provider is sent to a worker. This violates the requirement that local finders stay local and can make a time-limited finder wait for worker pickup.
findings.suggestion: Carry an explicit local-finder flag to the executor and exclude those calls from worker dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a free codex-cli provider and a panel finder marked local that selects its model, with review workers enabled for the repository. The executor enqueues the finder instead of running it locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 applies only `...(finder?.local ? { billing: "free_only" as const } : {})`; the shared call supplies `checkout` at engine.ts:1840–1843. src/router/config-catalog.ts:57–59 permits `kind: "codex-cli"` with `billing: "free"`. src/router/router.ts:192–196 adds backend fields only when endpoint URLs exist. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 accepts readonly reviews with checkout and no backend/openai/decisions, without checking local-finder intent or billing; line 157 calls `workers.enqueueAgentJob(request, id)`.
verification.trigger: Configure an endpoint-free, free codex-cli provider selected by a local panel finder, and enable review workers for the GitHub repository. The finder receives checkout metadata and passes worker eligibility, creating a worker job despite the requirement that local finders stay local.

findings.title: A pinned review model can send a local finder to a worker
findings.detail: Local finders receive the same checkout metadata as production finders. Their free-only routing constraint does not keep them local when the run pins a review model: the router lets a pinned chain override billing constraints. If that model uses a supported harness without backend credentials, the worker executor dispatches the local finder.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder designation to the dispatch decision, or omit checkout metadata for local finders. Add a panel test with a local finder and a pinned Claude or Codex review model.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub run enables worker reviews, configures a local panel finder, and pins a Claude review model. The local finder creates a worker job instead of running locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 marks a local finder only through `billing: "free_only"`; lines 1840–1843 nevertheless supply checkout metadata. src/pipeline/context.ts:545 uses `const chain = shadow ? undefined : this.run.models?.[opts.role as RunRole]`. src/router/router.ts:379–380 computes `const paid = !c.chain && c.billing !== undefined && m.billing !== "free" ? 1 : 0;`, so a pinned chain bypasses the free-only filter. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 permits that readonly Claude review call.
verification.trigger: A GitHub run with review workers enabled and a pinned Claude review model invokes a local panel finder. The pin bypasses its billing constraint, and the shared checkout metadata makes it eligible for worker dispatch.

findings.title: Validate hidden tests under the same cleanup conditions as grading
findings.detail: Validation runs the hidden command immediately after setup, leaving untracked setup artifacts in the worktree. The implement grader runs gates and then performs `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdq` before injecting hidden files. A case can therefore pass at head during generation but fail when graded. The new fixture itself uses a setup-created untracked `ready` file that grading would remove.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the grader's reset and clean before injecting and running hidden tests, and exercise an accepted case through the actual grading path.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup writes an untracked `ready` file and a hidden test reads it. Head validation passes, but grading removes `ready` before running the hidden command, so even the reference implementation fails.

The fixture itself creates `ready` at test/implement-replay-cases.test.ts:95 and reads it at :81.
verification.trigger: Setup creates an untracked, nonignored ready file needed by hidden tests. Generator validation accepts head, but grading deletes ready and the reference implementation fails.

findings.suggestion: Stage hidden files under a temporary name and make interrupted publication recoverable on the next run.

verification.trigger: Termination between creating the hidden directory and publishing cases.json leaves an orphan directory. Rerunning chooses the same ID and refuses to publish the case. The interruption window is a short synchronous sequence.

candidates.detail: Validation runs the hidden command immediately after setup, leaving untracked setup artifacts in the worktree. The implement grader runs gates and then performs `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdq` before injecting hidden files. A case can therefore pass at head during generation but fail when graded. The new fixture itself uses a setup-created untracked `ready` file that grading would remove.
candidates.suggestion: Mirror the grader's reset and clean before injecting and running hidden tests, and exercise an accepted case through the actual grading path.

candidates.title: Connect production complexity lookup in the CLI
candidates.detail: The only supported command-line entry point never supplies `lookupRun`, so every generated case defaults to medium even when the factory run record and its triage complexity are available. This also bypasses the explicit rejection of unsupported known complexities and can misclassify the tasks used for model comparison.

candidates.title: Recover from interruption while publishing hidden files

If the process stops during that interval, the orphaned hidden directory remains while the ID is absent from cases.json. Every subsequent run selects the same ID and refuses it because the directory already exists, preventing progress without manual cleanup.
candidates.suggestion: Stage hidden files under a temporary name and make interrupted publication recoverable on the next run.
candidates.failure_scenario: The process terminates after creating `hidden/impl-013` but before renaming the updated cases.json. Re-running the same PR reports that the hidden destination already exists and cannot add the case.

candidates.title: Wire production run lookup into the CLI

candidates.title: Return a failing exit status for operational errors
candidates.detail: The per-PR catch converts every exception into a table row, and the CLI exits successfully even if every PR failed because GitHub access, cache creation, or worktree validation failed. Automation relying on the exit status can therefore treat a generator run that produced nothing as successful.

candidates.failure_scenario: The gh command fails authentication for every requested PR; the table contains errors, but the generator exits with status 0.

candidates.title: The command never looks up production complexity
